body.heading: A new baby rearranges everyone
paragraphs: A new baby is joyful and disorienting at once, including for the people around the parents: grandparents finding their role, friends unsure how often to visit, an older child working out what has happened to their world. Gentleness in the first weeks is mostly about timing and scale.

Short visits, announced in advance, with food in hand and no expectation of being entertained, are the gold standard. Admire the baby, ask after the parents — in that order of novelty but not of importance.

body.heading: Help that actually helps
paragraphs: The useful offers are specific and unglamorous: a meal that only needs reheating, an hour of holding the baby while a parent showers or sleeps, laundry taken away and returned folded, the older child's trip to the park. Ask 'what would help this week?' and believe the answer, even if it is 'sleep and sandwiches'.
Advice, by contrast, is best served when ordered. New parents are flooded with it; a friend who mostly listens and admires becomes the one whose opinion gets asked for later.

body.heading: Remember the older children
paragraphs: A small present or an outing for a new big brother or sister — something that is theirs, in a week when everything is the baby's — can matter out of proportion to its size. They are having the biggest change of anyone.
Photograph them holding the baby if everyone is willing, and also photograph them alone, being splendid at their own thing. Both pictures will matter later.
